references.text: Moses wrote down this song on the same day and taught it to the Israelites, fulfilling God's command in verse 19.
The song itself that Moses was commanded to write down, known as the Song of Moses, which was to serve as a witness against the Israelites.
An earlier command to write something down as a memorial, a testimony for future generations.
The command to teach God's words to children and speak about them, parallel to teaching the song to the Israelites.
Explains the purpose of the song as a witness when many disasters and troubles strike the people.
God's command to proclaim His deeds to future generations, with a similar purpose to teaching the song to the Israelites.
A command to write on a tablet so it can serve as a witness for the future, parallel to writing down the song as testimony.
The prophet's command to clearly write down the vision so it can be preserved as testimony.
